title: Hybrid CCM in Thalassiosira pseudonana
projectDescription: Manipulated carbonate chemistry to disentangle proteins involved in the carbon concentrating mechanism (CCM) of Thalassiosira pseudonana from other cellular mechanisms that employ the same proteins.  The malate/oxaloacetate shuttle shares overlap with biochemical CCMs while also supporting pH regulation, maintenance of redox poise, cyclic electron transport, and the dissipation of excess light energy.  Three treatments were used to separate out the effects of pH and pCO2: low pCO2/high pH (LCHpH), high pCO2/low pH (HCLpH), and low pCO2/low pH (LCLpH).  Results from this analysis were consistent with a hybrid CCM within T. pseudonana that consists of both biophysical and biochemical steps.  No evidence for alternative cellular mechanisms that could explain protein abundance profiles observed under low pCO2 conditions was found.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Proteomic sample preparation followed the SP3 method by Hughes et al., 2014. Sample preparation and LC-MS/MS sequencing were completed by staff at the Biological Mass Spectrometry Facility of Robert Wood Johnson Medical School and Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey.  Protein extracts were reduced with DTT and stored at -80C before transit to the Biological Mass Spectrometry Facility.  10 ug total protein was diluted in 50 mM HEPES pH 8.0, 1% SDS, 50 mM EDTA, and 10 mM DTT.  Samples were denatured at 60C before addition of iodoacetamide.  A 1:1 mixture of Sera-Mag Carboxylate SpeedBeads E3 and E7 was added to each sample to a final ratio of 10:1 bead mixture to total protein.  Proteins were digested with 1:25 trypsin in 100 mM NH4HCO3, 2 mM CaCl2.   Peptide sequencing was completed with a Thermo Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid mass spectrometer with a Dionex U-3000 Rapid Separation nano LC system.
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS output files were Thermo .raw format and were processed with DIA-NN ver. 2.0.2 (Demichev et al., 2020; Kistner et al. [preprint]).  DIA-NN was run on the original FASTA sequences for a curated T. pseudonana reference library generated from Uniprot protein sequences and a universal contaminants library from Frankenfield et al., 2022, the in silico spectral library created from these FASTA libraries, and all 12 experimental data files.  The high precision Quant UMS quantification strategy was used with a precursor FDR of 1%, MBR enabled, and protein inference enabled.  All other parameters were set to the recommended default settings in the DIA-NN user manual.  Statistical contrasts of differential protein abundances were analyzed in R ver. 4.4.1 (R Core Team, 2024) using the MSqRob2 Bioconductor R package ver. 1.12.0 (Goeminne et al., 2016; Goeminne et al., 2020; Sticker et al., 2020) for robust ridge regression model fitting.  The Benjamini-Hochberg method to control FDR was used and differential protein abundances > 1.30-fold with an adjusted P < 0.05 were considered significant.
